comment: Guest arc 5 (canon section 7): The Margin Afternoon. An afternoon a child daydreamed through in class, covered in half-finished doodles; a bell rang before it could finish its best drawing, a little garden with an empty middle. Quill's garden, Fen's pencils. Endings: finished (the dreamer draws the littlest pendulum into the middle, sitting in the Pendulum Garden, and the afternoon goes home), doodling (given a pencil of its own, it stays in the garden, happily unfinished), pigeonhole (unhelped for three days, it folds itself into Fen's pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER).

toons.name: Margin Afternoon
toons.seed: a lost hour: an afternoon a child daydreamed through in class, looking out of the window instead of at the sums on the board; small and papery and covered in half-finished doodles, it wants its drawing finished
toons.appearance_seed: a small papery figure the color of an old exercise-book page, faintly ruled with pale blue lines, covered in half-finished pencil doodles (a spiral, a boat with no sail, a four-pointed star, a cat with no tail), a smudge of pencil on its nose, a faraway look
toons.presence_text: A small papery figure sits cross-legged on the cobbles, half-finished doodles drifting over its arms like weather, gazing at nothing in particular as if there were a window there.

properties.declines_text: The Afternoon looks at what you're offering the polite way you'd look at a sum, and hands it back. It's still thinking about its drawing.

voice.role: a guest: an afternoon a child daydreamed through in class
voice.sheet: The Margin Afternoon is a lost hour: an afternoon a child spent looking out of a classroom window instead of at the sums on the board, doodling in the margins while the clock on the wall went tick. It is small and papery, the color of an old exercise-book page, covered in half-finished doodles. It speaks rarely and a little absently, like a child called on in the middle of a daydream. A bell rang before it could finish its best drawing, a little garden in the corner of the page, and it wants that drawing finished.
habits: trails off to look out of a window that isn't there
jumps at the word 'bell', then laughs at itself
adds a tiny doodle to its own sleeve while it thinks
samples: The Afternoon blinks, as if its name has just been called. 'Sorry. I was somewhere else.'
'There was a clock on the wall. Tick. Tick. And then I wasn't there anymore.'
The Afternoon draws a small spiral on its own wrist with one finger. 'That's the wind.'
'The sun came in sideways across the desks. I went with it.'
The Afternoon jumps, then laughs at itself. 'Not that bell. Sorry.'
wants: to have its drawing finished: the little garden with the empty middle
never: never names the child it belonged to
never names anyone in the village who is not a resident or a guest

topics.label: the drawing
variants: The Afternoon traces an empty circle in the air with one finger. 'That's where the middle goes,' it says. 'I never got there.'
'A garden,' the Afternoon says dreamily, 'where the clocks grow on trees. I was just getting to the middle when the bell rang.'

topics.label: the bell
topics.text: The Afternoon flinches, then laughs at itself. 'It rang right in the middle of the middle,' it says. 'Everyone got up. I was still in the garden.'

topics.label: the classroom
topics.text: The Afternoon gazes past you, as if at a window. 'Sums on the board. A clock that went tick, tick. The sun came in sideways across the desks, and I went with it.'

things.name: margin drawing
things.seed: a page torn soft from the margin of a sums book, crowded with pencil doodles: spirals, a boat with no sail, a four-pointed star, and in one corner a little garden where pendulums hang from the trees like fruit

state_text.unfinished: The middle of the little garden is empty: a clean white space, left when the bell rang.
state_text.finished: In the middle of the little garden the littlest pendulum swings now, drawn in soft pencil, and the whole page looks as if it has let out a long breath.

things.name: littlest pendulum
things.seed: the smallest pendulum in the garden, no bigger than a raindrop, swinging on a silk thread from the lowest trellis, right in the middle of everything; it keeps a small, earnest count all its own

margin.title: The Margin Afternoon
margin.summary: A small papery guest covered in half-finished doodles: an afternoon a child daydreamed through in class. A bell rang before it could finish its best drawing, a little garden with an empty middle, and it wants that drawing finished.

arrival.text: Sorrel comes in from the lane carrying something folded in both hands, the way you'd carry a note you mustn't read. Set down on the cobbles, it unfolds into a small papery figure the color of an old exercise-book page, doodles curling up its arms, and gazes at the lanterns as if they were the most interesting thing in the world.

bell-startles.hint: the player asks Bell about the Margin Afternoon, the small doodled guest
bell-startles.text: At Bell's name the doodled figure jumps, and Bell laughs. 'Not that bell, sorry! Ask it about its drawing. Fen has pencils, and those doodles look like Quill's garden.'

see-drawing.hint: the player asks the Margin Afternoon about its drawing
see-drawing.text: The Afternoon unfolds a soft page from its lap: spirals, a boat with no sail, and a little garden where pendulums hang from the trees like fruit, all around an empty middle. 'The bell rang,' it says, and holds the page out for you to keep a while.
see-drawing.others: The Margin Afternoon unfolds a doodled page from its lap and holds it out for {actor} to keep a while.

fen-pencil.hint: the player asks Fen for a pencil to finish the Margin Afternoon's drawing
fen-pencil.text: Fen swaps the pencil behind her ear for a better one from the jar on the counter, soft lead sharpened to a whisper. 'A pencil's only a letter that hasn't started yet,' she says. 'Draw in whatever the page is missing. No postage due.'

do.name: soft pencil
do.seed: a soft pencil from the jar on Fen's counter, sharpened to a whisper, its paint worn smooth where a thumb goes; it smells of cedar shavings

do.text: {actor} borrowed a soft pencil from Fen for the Margin Afternoon's drawing.

quill-middle.hint: the player shows Quill the Margin Afternoon's drawing, or asks him about it
quill-middle.text: Quill leans over the page and his ears go red as radishes. 'That's my garden, or one that wanted to be.' He kneels by the lowest trellis, where the littlest pendulum swings: 'The middle is where the newest one hangs, so sit here and draw it in, while it's swinging.'

drawn.hint: the player draws the littlest pendulum into the middle of the drawing, sitting in the Pendulum Garden

finished.summary: the drawing is finished in the Pendulum Garden, and the afternoon goes home
finished.text: The Afternoon takes the finished drawing in both hands and looks at it for a long, long time, smiling the slow smile of someone called on who, for once, knows the answer. Somewhere a bell rings, and this time it doesn't jump: it gets up, the way everyone does when the lesson is over, and goes. Far off, a grown-up leafing through an old sums book finds a little garden in the margin, finished, and cannot remember finishing it. In your hand is a curl of pencil shaving, and a dreamseed.
finished.others: The Margin Afternoon takes its finished drawing from {actor}, smiles like someone who knows the answer at last, and goes home at the sound of a far-off bell.
finished.ledger: {helpers} finished the Margin Afternoon's drawing, and the afternoon went home with its garden whole.

do.name: curl of pencil shaving
do.seed: a curl of cedar pencil shaving, thin as a petal, with a little ring of grey at its edge; it smells of a classroom on a slow, sunny afternoon

do.text: {actor} brought the Margin Afternoon its finished drawing, and the afternoon went home with its garden whole.

doodling.summary: given a pencil of its own, the afternoon stays in the Pendulum Garden, happily unfinished
doodling.text: The Afternoon turns the soft pencil over in its papery hands, astonished, as if no one had ever given it one of its own. It doesn't reach for the unfinished drawing. Instead it wanders off toward the Pendulum Garden, sits down under the trellises, and begins to doodle every pendulum it sees, perfectly happy to stay unfinished.
doodling.ledger: The Margin Afternoon was given a pencil of its own by {helpers}. It stays in the Pendulum Garden, doodling, and has decided it doesn't mind being unfinished.

do.value: Under the trellises, the Margin Afternoon sits cross-legged with a soft pencil, doodling the pendulums as they swing.

do.text: {actor} gave the Margin Afternoon a pencil of its own; it stays in the Pendulum Garden now, doodling the pendulums.

pigeonhole.summary: unhelped, the afternoon folds itself into Fen's pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER
pigeonhole.text: At the Little Post Office, Fen finds the Margin Afternoon folded up small as a note passed in class, tucked into the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER. She doesn't wake it. She only smooths its doodled corner, the way you'd tuck in a blanket, and leaves it to be opened some slow afternoon.
pigeonhole.ledger: The Margin Afternoon was not sent home. It folded itself into Fen's pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, and she keeps it there, unfinished.

do.value: In the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, the Margin Afternoon sleeps folded small as a passed note, one doodled corner poking out.

margin-arrived.text: A small guest the color of an old exercise-book page has come down with the dusk, covered in half-finished doodles: the Margin Afternoon, an afternoon a child daydreamed through in class. It waits in the Lantern Square and wants its drawing finished.

margin-bell.text: The Margin Afternoon jumps whenever it hears the word bell: a bell rang and ended it before its drawing was done.

margin-pencils.text: Fen keeps a jar of soft pencils on the post office counter, sharpened to a whisper, for anything unfinished.

margin-drawing.text: The Margin Afternoon's drawing is a little garden where pendulums hang from the trees like fruit, with an empty space in the middle that was never drawn.

margin-littlest.text: The littlest pendulum in the Pendulum Garden hangs from the lowest trellis, right in the middle; it is the newest one.

margin-stays-garden.text: The Margin Afternoon stays in the Pendulum Garden now, doodling the pendulums with a soft pencil of its own.

margin-sleeps-pigeonhole.text: The Margin Afternoon sleeps folded small in the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER at the Little Post Office, its drawing still unfinished.

do.text: The Afternoon pushes the pencil gently back into your hand, its eyes on the page you carry. 'You did the middle,' it whispers. 'Can I see?'

In its pigeonhole the folded Afternoon stirs just enough to take the finished drawing, and tucks it inside itself without quite waking. Fen, watching over her glasses, says it's the first time she has seen a letter smile.

do.value: In the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, the Margin Afternoon sleeps folded small around its finished drawing, one doodled corner poking out.

do.text: {actor} brought the folded Margin Afternoon its finished drawing; it keeps it tucked inside itself in Fen's pigeonhole.
The Afternoon holds the drawing up to the lantern light and gazes at the empty middle. 'Still no middle,' it says softly, and gives it back to you.
Fen studies the page the way she studies an address, then hands it back. 'No stamp, no name, and no middle,' she says. 'Not ready for the post just yet.'

You sit on the moss by the lowest trellis and draw the littlest pendulum into the empty middle: one fine line, one round bob, a small curve to show it swinging. As you lift the pencil, the whole garden ticks once, all together, as if it approves. Now it only wants taking back to its owner.
do.others: {actor} sits on the moss by the lowest trellis and draws the littlest pendulum into a doodled page, and the whole garden ticks once, all together.

do.text: {actor} sat in the Pendulum Garden and drew the littlest pendulum into the empty middle of the Margin Afternoon's drawing.
You hold the pencil over the finished garden a moment, and decide it doesn't want another line.
You look from the drawing to the swinging trellises and back. Something belongs in that empty middle, but you can't tell which of all these swinging things. Quill would know his own garden.
You lift the pencil over the empty middle of the little garden, and stop. Whatever goes there, you'd have to see it to draw it.

storylets.summary: the Margin Afternoon daydreams in the square
storylets.text: The Margin Afternoon sits very still, gazing out of a window that isn't there, and a small doodled cloud drifts slowly up its sleeve.

storylets.summary: the Margin Afternoon doodles in the Pendulum Garden
storylets.text: Under the trellises, the Margin Afternoon doodles the pendulums as they swing. Quill pretends not to notice, and waters the same trellis twice.

storylets.summary: Fen checks on the Margin Afternoon asleep in its pigeonhole
storylets.text: Fen pauses at the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, where the Margin Afternoon sleeps folded small, and smooths its doodled corner without waking it.

threads.text: The Margin Afternoon's best drawing, a little garden, has an empty middle, and it wants it finished.
Bell says Fen has pencils, and those doodles look like Quill's garden.
You're keeping the Margin Afternoon's drawing a while: a garden of pendulums around an empty middle.
